message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"96116245c5840bb29b75fe2475ea9cc87afe41303376f54692e44b1c9ca976ec","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-va-class-std:lineage:89","source_registry_sha256":"b6300aba50e85a8fd509daf2f853e3d2d116b38a9707baf75df5057c8071f937","units":[{"unit_id":"sec07-u01","module_id":"sec07-m01","objective_ids":["sec07-u01"],"title":{"text":"Yielding at intersections","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections; private-road and driveway entries require stopping before yielding to all traffic and pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02"]},{"text":"Left turns yield to opposing traffic, and simultaneous arrivals without signs or signals give priority to the driver on the right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ivy and another driver reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same moment, and the other car is on Ivy's right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Where uncontrolled roads meet with simultaneous arrivals, you yield to the vehicle on your right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"result":{"text":"Ivy yields and lets the car on her right go first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a plain green light lets a left turn go ahead of oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Before making the left turn, give way to vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians approaching from the opposite direction.","fact_ids":["sec07-R01","sec07-F02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Same-time arrivals without signals: right first.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Ivy and another driver arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, and the other car is on her right. Who goes first?","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},"answer":{"text":"The car on Ivy's right; she yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"rationale":{"text":"The example specifies simultaneous arrival without signs or signals, so the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who goes first","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Marked and unmarked crossing duties.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Private entries require a stop and yield.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Left turns and simultaneous arrivals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on right-of-way at crossings and private-road entries. Yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections. Entering from a private road or driveway adds a required stop before yielding to all traffic and pedestrians. A left turn gives way to opposing traffic, and simultaneous arrivals at an intersection without signs or signals use the right-hand rule. These conditions matter, so identify the kind of entry, turn or arrival in the question before choosing who proceeds. The following examples keep each stated rule in its own context.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Crossings and private entries","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yield at marked or unmarked intersections.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Private-road or driveway entry: stop.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Yield to all traffic and pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Yield to pedestrians crossing in marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections. If you are joining the roadway from a private road or driveway, first stop, then yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Keep the added stop requirement in mind. A question about a private driveway asks more than whether you should watch for another vehicle; it also requires a stop before entry. In a practice situation, a driver waits at a private driveway while a pedestrian crosses and roadway traffic passes. The driver applies the private-entry rule without treating the driveway as priority over the road.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Left turns yield","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Check that the path is clear.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Yield to traffic approaching from the opposite direction.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Include bicycles and pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"When making a left turn, give way to traffic approaching from the opposite direction. The cited page includes bicycles and pedestrians in that check. Even after you have looked for a clear path, do not treat your intention to turn as priority over opposing traffic. For a practice example, an approaching bicycle is moving through the intersection while you intend to turn left. Let it pass before completing the turn. The rule is about yielding during the left turn. Keep that duty separate from assumptions about a signal granting an unconditional right-of-way.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01","sec07-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Simultaneous arrival without signals","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"No signs or signals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"Vehicles arrive at the same time.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"The driver on the left yields right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"The stated right-hand rule applies when vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection without signs or signals. The driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first. Check all parts of the situation: the intersection has no signs or signals, the arrivals are simultaneous, and one driver is positioned to the other driver's right. In the practice example, Ivy sees another car on her right as both reach the intersection together. Ivy yields. Do not replace the stated conditions with an unrelated junction rule; use the arrival and position described.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Protect people crossing","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Red-light turns need particular care.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing within marked crosswalks or at unmarked intersections must be allowed to cross safely. The manual warns that turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians. That warning reinforces the crossing duty; it is not permission to turn without checking. In a practice situation, a person is crossing while a driver is considering a turn. The driver yields and lets that person finish safely. Identify the crossing and the people using it rather than treating a turn as priority over them. Keep attention on the crossing throughout the turn decision.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the arrival","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"No signs or signals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"Both vehicles arrive together.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"The other car is on your right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Ivy and another driver reach an intersection without signs or signals at the same moment. The other vehicle is on Ivy's right. Who goes first? The car on the right goes first, and Ivy yields. The example supplies the conditions for the stated rule: no signs or signals and simultaneous arrival. Position then decides which driver yields. Read those details before answering, instead of relying on a different type of intersection from memory. The concise recall line is: at the same time without signals, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Yield rules recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yield to people crossing.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Private entries stop and yield.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Left turns yield; same-time arrivals give way right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To recap, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists at marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections. Joining from a private road or driveway requires a stop and yielding to all traffic and pedestrians. A left turn yields to traffic approaching from the opposite direction, including bicycles and pedestrians. If vehicles arrive together at an intersection without signs or signals, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right. Turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians, so do not lose sight of the crossing duty while deciding about a turn. Apply each rule with its stated conditions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u02","module_id":"sec07-m02","objective_ids":["sec07-u02"],"title":{"text":"Emergency vehicles and crossing duties","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"why_how":[{"text":"For an emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren or flashing lights, yield, pull safely to the right edge, stop and wait until it passes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Stopped emergency vehicles or tow trucks with flashing lights call for a safe lane change or cautious slowdown; marked and unmarked crossings require yielding to pedestrians and bicyclists.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sara approaches a tow truck stopped with flashing lights.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights requires cautious travel and, when reasonable and safe, a move to a nonadjacent lane; otherwise reduce speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"result":{"text":"Sara changes lanes away from the vehicle, or slows to a safe speed if she cannot change lanes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a stopped vehicle with flashers requires the same full stop as an approaching siren.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"Active sirens and lights demand pulling over, stopping and waiting, while stopped flashers demand only a lane move or a safe slowdown.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06","sec07-F07"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Moving siren: pull over; stopped lights: move over.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Sara approaches a stopped tow truck with flashing lights. What does the rule require?","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},"answer":{"text":"Change lanes away or slow to a safe speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"Stopped flashers demand a lane move or a safe slowdown, while active sirens demand pulling over and stopping.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Making way","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"An emergency vehicle approaches from behind.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},{"text":"A stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]},{"text":"Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson separates an approaching emergency vehicle from a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights. One situation requires pulling over and stopping; the other uses the lane-change or cautious slowdown rule explained next.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Moving versus stopped","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Approaching from behind: right edge, stop, wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck: cautious travel.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Change lanes safely, or reduce speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"For a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights, proceed cautiously. Also keep the stopped-truck situation distinct from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren, where the response is pulling to the right edge and stopping. Moving siren, pull over; stopped lights, move over.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Making way recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Emergency behind: right edge, stop and wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Stopped emergency or tow truck: move safely or slow.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Yield at marked and unmarked crossings.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, yield to an emergency vehicle approaching from behind with a siren or flashing lights, pull safely to the right edge and stop until it passes. Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections must be allowed to cross safely. Moving siren, pull over; stopped lights, move over. Stay in your lane until ready to exit, and use the right turn signal to show your intention.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"rationale":{"text":"Remaining in the lane until exit readiness is the stated roundabout rule.","fact_ids":["sec07-R08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Inside the circle","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow and yield on entry.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise travel.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Lanes, exits and trucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on roundabouts. A roundabout is a circular intersection with a center island, and it has a small set of rules that cover entering, circulating and leaving. You enter by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, and yielding to crossing pedestrians. You travel counterclockwise around the island. Inside, remain in your lane until ready to exit and use your right turn signal to indicate your intention. In this lesson we take those rules one at a time, and we end with a trap about who yields when you enter the circle.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Entering","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow down.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Yield to every circulating lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Yield to crossing pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Enter a roundabout by slowing down and yielding to every circulating lane. Then circle counterclockwise around the island, and yield to crossing pedestrians. Note the words every circulating lane. In a roundabout with more than one lane, you yield to traffic in all of them, not just the lane nearest to you. And the pedestrian yield from the intersection rules applies here too: pedestrians crossing at the roundabout are yielded to. The direction of travel is fixed: counterclockwise around the island. Entry is about patience: slow, yield to the circle and to pedestrians, then join.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Keep your lane and signal","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stay in your lane until ready to exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Use the right signal to show your intention.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Inside a roundabout, stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. Use the right turn signal to show the drivers around you what you intend to do. Keep lane position and signaling together in your recall. A driver who is not yet ready to exit stays in the current lane rather than treating the circle as permission for an unnecessary lane change. When preparing to leave, the right signal communicates the intended movement. This is the stated guidance for traveling inside the roundabout. Keep lane position and the right signal together when recalling the stated inside-the-circle guidance.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Entry yields to the circle","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Entering traffic yields.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Circulating traffic keeps moving.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise, signed lanes, right-turn exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap: some drivers think the cars already in the roundabout must make room for them as they enter. It is the other way around. Roundabout entry yields to every circulating lane, while circulating means counterclockwise travel, signed lane choice and a right-turn exit. The traffic in the circle has the right-of-way, and you join it only after yielding to every circulating lane. Once you are circulating, you keep to your signed lane, travel counterclockwise, and leave with a right turn. If an exam question asks who yields at a roundabout, the answer is the driver entering, to every circulating lane and to crossing pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F09","sec07-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the exit","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Noor is inside the roundabout.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"She is not yet ready to exit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Should she stay in her lane?","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Noor is traveling inside a roundabout and is not yet ready to exit. Should she remain in her lane? Yes. The manual says to stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. She uses the right turn signal when indicating her intention to leave. This check focuses on lane position inside the circle, rather than introducing a separate rule about a particular vehicle beside her. The example asks about a driver who is already inside and is not yet ready to leave. Use the lane rule for that stage of travel. Noor applies the lane rule to the stage of the trip described in the question.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Roundabout recap","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow, yield to every circulating lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Counterclockwise around the island.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Signed lanes, right-turn exit, room for trucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close the lesson: enter a roundabout by slowing, yielding to every circulating lane, and yielding to crossing pedestrians. Travel counterclockwise around the center island. Inside, pick your lane by signs and arrows, and exit with a right turn. Remain in your lane until ready to exit, and use your right turn signal.
